title: Teenagers and a TV programme: independence

source.note: Stem text verbatim from the QP PDF; steps and marks from the official MS PDF (UCLES 2011). Part (i) (union of ‘female’ and ‘watches Kops are Kids’) is outside this section and is omitted. The official MS also allows a conditional-probability comparison; that alternative is recorded, but the primary method here is the product P(M)P(W).

stem: In a group of 30 teenagers, 13 of the 18 males watch ‘Kops are Kids’ on television and 3 of the 12 females watch ‘Kops are Kids’.

steps.name: prod
steps.note: MS: M1 valid attempt to find P(M), P(W) and P(M)×P(W).

steps.name: cmp
steps.text_tex: \(\mathrm{P}(M\text{ and }W)=\dfrac{13}{30}\neq\dfrac{8}{25}\), so the events are not independent.
steps.note: MS: A1 P(M and W)=13/30 ≠ 8/25 and correct conclusion. Alternative (official): P(M|W)=(13/30)/(16/30)=13/16 ≠ 18/30=P(M), not independent.

title: Two dice: total 5 and low/high scores, independence

source.note: Stem text verbatim from the QP PDF; steps and marks from the official MS PDF (UCLES 2013). Official alternatives include P(S|Q)=P(S) or P(Q|S)=P(Q); the primary method taught in this section is the product comparison. Official MS final answer: independent, since P(Q∩S)=2/36 = P(Q)×P(S).

stem: \(Q\) is the event ‘Nicola throws two fair dice and gets a total of 5’. \(S\) is the event ‘Nicola throws two fair dice and gets one low score (1, 2 or 3) and one high score (4, 5 or 6)’. Are events \(Q\) and \(S\) independent? Justify your answer.

steps.name: pq
steps.text_tex: Outcomes for a total of 5: \((1,4),\,(2,3),\,(3,2),\,(4,1)\), so \(\mathrm{P}(Q)=\dfrac{4}{36}\). Outcomes for one low and one high: \(3\times3\times2=18\), so \(\mathrm{P}(S)=\dfrac{18}{36}=\dfrac12\).

steps.name: cmp
steps.note: MS: M1 comparing a correct pair of terms (product, or a conditional with the marginal), with all probabilities in [0,1).

steps.name: con
steps.note: MS: A1 Independent, provided all the probabilities used are correct.

title: Two dice: independence and mutually exclusive

source.note: Stem text verbatim from the QP PDF; steps and marks from the official MS PDF (UCLES 2015). Part (i) is the independence test for this section. Part (ii) is mutually exclusive (taught in S1-4.2) and is kept because it is the official remainder of the same question.

stem: Jason throws two fair dice, each with faces numbered 1 to 6. Event \(A\) is ‘one of the numbers obtained is divisible by 3 and the other number is not divisible by 3’. Event \(B\) is ‘the product of the two numbers obtained is even’.

steps.name: PA
steps.note: MS: M1 sensible attempt at P(A).

steps.name: PB
steps.note: MS: M1 sensible attempt at P(B).

steps.name: PAB
steps.note: MS: B1 correct P(A∩B).

steps.name: cmp
steps.note: MS: M1 compare P(A∩B) with P(A)×P(B); need at least one of these correct.

steps.name: con
steps.text_tex: The events are independent, since \(\mathrm{P}(A\cap B)=\mathrm{P}(A)\times\mathrm{P}(B)\).
steps.note: MS: A1 correct conclusion following all correct working.

steps.name: mex
steps.text_tex: (ii) Not mutually exclusive, because \(\mathrm{P}(A\cap B)\neq0\) (for example, the outcome \((1,6)\) belongs to both events).
steps.note: MS: B1 [1] ft their P(A∩B). Or give a counter-example, e.g. 1 and 6.
